tokenizer_dependency_optional._comment: DO NOT set this unless your team genuinely tokenizes EVERY pretrain corpus with one canonical tokenizer. Tokenizers vary per dataset, so the primary path is per-dataset: pass tokenizer="tokenizer/<name>" to publish() for each corpus. A family-wide default is dangerous precisely because a wrong tokenizer is hard to detect - vocab sizes are similar (~100k) so a mismatched tokenizer's ids usually still fall in range and the decode check passes while being semantically wrong. Only if standardized: set {role: tokenizer, dataset_id, version, manifest_sha256} of a published tokenizer/v1 dataset and publish() will attach it to any corpus that does not name its own.

notes: Packed token shards ready to feed straight into OLMo-core pretraining runs: the raw fuel, in training order-agnostic form, with a tokenizer pinned hard enough that token counts are falsifiable. Names carry corpus plus token budget, because the budget is the axis that distinguishes siblings (pretrain/dolma2-150b, pretrain/fineweb-edu-10b) - see DATASET-STANDARD.md section 2. THE FORMAT DEFAULT IS THE POINT: uint32 little-endian, headerless, extension .u32le.bin, NEVER .npy. OLMo-core memmaps these files from byte 0 (olmo_core/data/utils.py:158) and derives token count from raw file size (:233), so a real 128-byte .npy header would corrupt the leading tokens AND the count, silently. OLMo-core also defaults to dtype uint16 while these corpora are uint32, which halves the count if dtype is inferred rather than read - hence dtype is declared here and read by dataset_paths(), never guessed. THE TOKENIZER IS A PUBLISHED DEPENDENCY, NAMED PER DATASET, NOT A HAND-TYPED PIN OR A FAMILY DEFAULT: there is no single canonical tokenizer for this family - different corpora use different tokenizers - so each corpus NAMES its own by passing tokenizer="tokenizer/<name>" to publish() (publish it once with profile tokenizer/v1, then reference it). publish() pins it by manifest_sha256 and attaches it as the corpus's depends_on. The validator DERIVES vocab_size and eos_token_id from THAT published tokenizer.json (tokenizer_v1.derive_vocab) and the decode smoke test asserts every sampled id against the derived vocab_size (0 <= id < vocab_size) - computed from the real tokenizer this corpus actually used, never a guess and never a shared default that might not match. tokenizer_dependency_optional above is OFF by default and should stay that way unless a team genuinely standardizes on one tokenizer for every corpus - a wrong family-wide default is dangerous precisely because a mismatched tokenizer's ids usually still fall in range and pass silently. This replaces the old inline vocab_size/eos_token_id pins, which were unverifiable typed values. license.basis is an honest 'unknown' at the family level rather than a convenient 'ODC-By-1.0': this family will hold Dolma2 (ODC-By-1.0), FineWeb-Edu (ODC-By-1.0), and selection-method rebuilds of sources whose terms nobody has read, and section 3 is explicit that an honest unknown beats a false value and stays queryable in the catalog. Each dataset overrides license with its actual, checked terms. Per section 5 there is no -of-NNNNN in shard names: the surviving shard count is unknowable at write time because it depends on filtering that has not run yet; completeness is proven by path-set equality against the manifest instead. decode_smoke_test bounds are the section 7 defaults - they catch all-zeros shards, all-EOS shards, and the zero-filled tail a crashed writer leaves behind, all of which pass every checksum and size gate ever written.
